notes: Routing note: all five criteria are Yes, and this is not a PDCA-sized problem -- there is no single obvious fix (intake spec errors, prepress file problems, press smudge, and finishing trim all put orders on the reprint shelf), the metric is a defect rate that needs a real baseline window before anyone can claim improvement, and the money case rests on a quarter of reprint records. Route: full DMAIC.

scope_narrow.detail: First-presentation rejects on produced print orders at the campus print shop, both shifts (day and evening), Monday-Saturday -- not the self-serve copiers, not the mail room, not jobs brokered to the off-campus vendor.

measurable_outcome.detail: Binary per order at the QC desk -- accepted or rejected at first presentation against four named checks (paper stock, trim, ink, quantity) -- tracked as a daily proportion defective. Lower is better; attribute data, so the baseline is a p-chart, not an I-MR chart.

data_obtainable.detail: The QC desk already keeps a reject log (it is how the ~9% figure was noticed), job travelers carry per-step initials and rework marks, and a late-June pre-study week confirmed the log can be tallied daily by shift without slowing handoff.

process_owner_engaged.detail: Tessa Nguyen, day-shift lead, runs the QC desk and asked for the project after a 90-packet course order came back for crooked trim in June; Elaine Foster, campus print services manager, sponsors it.

business_impact_plausible.detail: Q2 2026 records put reprint materials, press and operator time on reprints, rush courier runs, and customer credits near $6,000 for the quarter -- roughly $24,000 a year if nothing changes.
